chapter_colophon: इति श्रीदामोदरसूनुना शार्ङ्गधरेण विरचितायां शार्ङ्गधरसंहितायां पूर्वखण्डे कलादिकाख्यानं नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः।।५।।

source_reconciliation.finding: The printed Dīpikā edition identifies Chapter 5 as Kalādikākhyānam and runs continuously to verse 122. The online Wikisource representation visibly compresses the middle of the chapter in search extraction, showing verse 1-3 and then later verse 71-73; therefore it is not safe to treat the compact extraction as a complete verse transcript.
source_reconciliation.resolution: Printed Dīpikā 1-122 is the canonical working extent. Full verse-level Sanskrit transcription should be taken from the page scans/text of the printed witness before final canonical import.
source_reconciliation.important_examples: BharatKosha page 74 shows verses 1-3; page 77 shows verse 29; page 83 includes verse 121; page 88 shows verses 120-122 and the colophon.
source_reconciliation.no_invention: No missing Sanskrit verses are reconstructed from memory or from parallel Saṃhitās.

verified_specific_points.point: Seven kalā, āśaya, dhātu, dhātumala, upadhātu and tvak are enumerated.
Three doṣa, 900 snāyu, 210 sandhi and 360 asthi are stated in the printed witness.
500 māṃsapeśī are stated for men; the printed commentary continues with female-specific counts and 16 kaṇḍarā.
Seven upadhātu are completed with sweat, teeth, hair and ojas among the listed products.
Lobha is defined in the printed text as craving arising on seeing/hearing another's property, enjoyments or capability.
Bondage is linked to ignorance, liberation to self-knowledge; disease is associated with suffering and health with सुख.

commentary_mapping.coverage: Dīpikā provides explanatory anatomy-style notes for the numerical enumeration and cross-references Suśruta Śārīrasthāna for kalā.
Dīpikā explains the seven kalā, āśaya and dhātu/upadhātu concepts; source-attributed traditional anatomy is kept distinct from modern anatomy.
Dīpikā explains tvak and marma categories with traditional terminology and location descriptions.
Dīpikā explains śirā, dhamanī, snāyu, asthi and sandhi according to the classical framework.
Dīpikā expands structural and psychophysical concepts and uses cross-Saṃhitā references.
Dīpikā explains anger, greed, bondage, liberation, disease and health; these explanations remain commentary, not canonical text.

assessments.question: शार्ङ्गधरसंहिता के मुद्रित पाठ में मर्म की संख्या कितनी बतायी गयी है?
अध्याय के प्रारम्भिक गणना-भाग में रसवहिनी धमनियों की संख्या कितनी दी गयी है?
सप्त कला का पारम्परिक ढाँचा क्या है और कलाओं को धातु/आशय से कैसे जोड़ा गया है?
शास्त्रीय संख्या-वर्णनों को आधुनिक anatomical counts के साथ पढ़ते समय किन स्रोत-सीमाओं को ध्यान में रखना चाहिए?
अध्याय के अंतिम श्लोक में व्याधि और आरोग्य का सम्बन्ध कैसे व्यक्त हुआ है?

canonical_import_plan.step_1: Transcribe printed Sanskrit verses 1-122 directly from the verified BharatKosha page scans.
canonical_import_plan.step_2: Cross-check verses against Wikisource wherever the online witness is complete.
canonical_import_plan.step_3: Preserve printed numbering and do not normalize traditional anatomical counts.
canonical_import_plan.step_4: Add Hindi translation only after Sanskrit sequence is locked.
canonical_import_plan.step_5: Map Dīpikā commentary without reproducing copyrighted commentary verbatim.
canonical_import_plan.step_6: Run canonical sequence, translation, commentary, assessment and reader regression gates.
